title: Qubits
intro: The two-level system that every QRC spin reservoir is made of: its geometry on the Bloch sphere, the Pauli operators that measure and rotate it, and the gates and circuits that run reservoirs on quantum computers.

blocks.text: A qubit is the simplest quantum system that is not classical: a two-dimensional state space. Real qubits are spin-1/2 nuclei (NMR), two levels of an atom (Rydberg arrays, trapped ions) or two levels of a superconducting circuit. The mathematics is the same for all of them, and the Pauli operators $X$, $Y$, $Z$ are its whole alphabet.

items: The Qubit and the Bloch Sphere (#/quantum/qubits/bloch-sphere): every pure qubit state as a point on a sphere, and what the coordinates mean.
Pauli Operators and Rotations (#/quantum/qubits/pauli-and-rotations): the Pauli algebra and rotations $R_P(\theta) = e^{-i\theta P/2}$, including the rotation that encodes an input into a qubit.
Gates and Circuits (#/quantum/qubits/gates-and-circuits): the Hadamard and CNOT, building an $XX$ coupling from two CNOTs, and Trotter steps for simulating a Hamiltonian on a gate-based device.
M. A. Nielsen and I. L. Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information, 10th anniversary edition, Cambridge University Press (2010), chapters 1 and 4
